problem: Existing simulators focus on static scenes, and existing dynamic pedestrian simulators have monotonous pedestrian models, no interaction with the environment and constrained scenarios. This leaves a large gap from real-world dynamic pedestrian settings for visual navigation.
motivation: Visual navigation in real environments must handle diverse pedestrian behaviors, but current benchmarks do not capture them, so evaluation and training are unrealistic. A more realistic, easily deployable pedestrian simulator, together with a baseline that handles moving people, is needed.
key_idea: Build DP-Habitat, a Habitat-based dynamic pedestrian simulator with diverse, environment-interactive human behaviors, and propose the AON-DM baseline, which combines pedestrian tracking and prediction with hybrid path planning for object navigation.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablations can be cited. The abstract claims that dynamic pedestrians significantly degrade visual navigation performance in DP-Habitat, and that explicit pedestrian tracking and prediction with dynamic mapping improves success and efficiency.
method: DP-Habitat simulator: a dynamic pedestrian simulator built on Habitat that simulates diverse, complex human behaviors with flexible pedestrian-environment interaction.
Rapid pedestrian deployment: supports fast placement of pedestrian models across various scenes.
AON-DM (Adaptive Object Navigation with Dynamic Mapping): a baseline for object navigation in dynamic pedestrian settings.
Real-time pedestrian tracking and predictive modeling: tracks pedestrians and predicts their motion within the map.
Hybrid path planning: combines planning strategies to avoid pedestrians and improve navigation efficiency.
